summary: Ugyen Pelgen is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned a master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

Ulrich Pagel specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski and teachers Philip Denwood and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, later holding a post at SOAS University of London (attested 2013–2020).

Ulrich Timme Kragh studied at the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute and the University of Copenhagen. Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, he held appointments at Copenhagen, Harvard, Geumgang University, IIAS, the University of Sydney, and ANU.

A scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology, Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff studied at Schulpforta, Bonn, and Berlin under Otto Jahn, Moriz Haupt, and Johannes Schmidt. He served as professor at Greifswald (1876–1883), Göttingen (1883–1897), and Berlin (1897–1921).

Ulrike Roesler, a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD from the University of Münster. She taught Indian and Tibetan studies at Marburg and Freiburg before becoming Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Oxford (attested 2019).

Uma Chakravarti is a historian working in history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, Mount Carmel College, Bangalore Institute of Legal Studies, and Delhi under D. Devahuti, later teaching at Miranda House (1966–1998).

Umakant Premanand Shah was an Indologist and historian. He served at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, as deputy director (1954) and head of the Ramayana Project (1965), and directed Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1954–1975).

Umesha Mishra was an Indologist and philosopher. He held a post at the University of Allahabad (~1923–1959), was founder secretary of Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha (~1943), and directed the Mithila Institute (~1951–1956).

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana studied at Bharathiar University and the University of Amsterdam. Working in Indology and related fields, he held posts at FRLHT, Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and the University of Toyama as a visiting researcher and associate professor.

Unrai Wogihara studied at Jōdo Shūgaku Honkō and Strasbourg under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, he taught at Tokyo, Shukyo University, Shiba Junior & Senior High School, and Taisho University.
Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded Juzen-kai (1884), Kairitsu Gakkō, and Juuzen Hokutsu.

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed specializes in Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She earned her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London and held an appointment as a research associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at the University of Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem studied at Mongolian State University of Arts and Culture, Eötvös Loránd University, and UC Berkeley (PhD). A specialist in history, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, she held positions at Berkeley, Yonsei, National University of Mongolia, and Indiana University.

Uranchimeg Tsultemin specializes in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. from UC Berkeley, where she lectured in the Art History Department, and served as an associate professor at the National University of Mongolia.

Urs App studied at Fribourg, Kyoto, and Temple University under Victor H. Mair, Yoshitaka Iriya, Richard DeMartino, and Seizan Yanagida. Working in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he held posts at Hanazono University, SNF, and EFEO.
Usharbudh Arya was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed studies at the University of London and held a post at the University of Minnesota from approximately 1967 to 1973.

Ute Hüsken studied at Göttingen under Heinz Bechert and completed her habilitation at Heidelberg. A scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, she held posts at Göttingen, Heidelberg, and the University of Oslo (2007–2017).

Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Vienna (1965–1972). He served as a university lecturer in Indology at Vienna from 1969 and completed a research stay at the University of Madras (1972–1974).

Indologist V. Raghavan studied under Sengalipuram Appaswamy Shastrigal and S. Kuppuswami Sastri at the University of Madras (PhD 1934). He worked in the Madras Sanskrit Department (1934–1968), founded the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and was secretary of Madras Music Academy.

Indologist V. S. Sukthankar studied at St. Xavier's, St John's, Edinburgh, and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, Hermann Jacobi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served with the Archaeological Survey of India and as Mahabharata General Editor at BORI.
